title: How to organize the paper and household backstock | Hall Closet
description:
Keeps a reserve of paper goods, bulbs, and batteries so you never make a late-night emergency trip.

This is the Paper and Household Backstock in the Hall Closet. About 30-45 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
Toilet roll in one clear bin with a card on the shelf edge reading "min 6, max 24". Bulbs in a labeled bin sorted by fitting. Batteries standing in their original packs in a shallow tray, sizes readable without lifting one out. Every bin label facing the door.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Take the lot out. Loose batteries you cannot vouch for, bulbs for fittings you replaced when you went over to
Straighten: Toilet roll goes into the clear bin loose so you can see the level drop, bulbs stay in their boxes grouped by
Shine: Wipe the shelf and check the tray bottom for the white crust that means a cell has leaked.
Safety: Loose batteries whose terminals touch metal or each other can short and heat up, and a button cell dropped on
Standardize: The minimum and maximum go on the shelf edge in front of each bin, not in your head.
Sustain: Lifting the last toilet roll out of the bin is the moment you are below the minimum, and it goes on the list b

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
Every bin carries a minimum and maximum on the shelf edge, stock is dated with a marker on arrival, and the oldest pack is pulled first.
